summary: The Merge fed this instance in as verdict rows only, so the rows an unreadable boot-repair run withdrew counted as measured corroboration with nothing said. The report's inputs now carry repair_record_unreadable (and the run ids) for this instance and for an uploaded export JSON, and the Merge panel writes the warning beside the numbers (one string, 12 locales); the merge still runs and refuses nothing. The warning also survives an uploaded all-diagnostics bundle and the panel's own YAML export (a top-level basis key, written only when the record was unreadable; load_overlay ignores it); the command-line merge does not show it. Rule 12 = b, carried out: repair_still_followed now ignores a judging attempt that merged_rows names (a backup merge inserted it), so only a later attempt this install made turns a repaired row measured in the export, the provenance page and the Merge. No migration, no backfill: a row whose judging attempts all came through a tracked merge, or a repaired row whose newer attempt did, goes from measured to inherited at its next export. The same rule now decides every judged row, not only repaired ones: a source whose whole judging history a merge brought in exports and reads as inherited, never measured (it used to ship as this install's own; a catalogue row that took a merged verdict reads inherited, not curated; the overlay editor no longer calls an imported newer attempt judged here (own imported_since label, one string x12) still declines to revert it, and never reverts a verdict a merge gave a row; a restore of the install's own backup reads inherited, with a proposal in OPEN_QUEUE). The residue (an imported attempt with no merged_rows row: a batch removed by hand in the database) reads as local and is pinned by a test. Each fix has a test that fails when it is removed.
